The trial enrolled four hundred eighty eight patients with a median age of fifty one, and two hundred twenty four who achieved MRD negative CR were randomized one to one across sites in the US, Canada, and Israel, with about twenty percent in each arm proceeding to autologous transplant. This is the study design slide, the actual survival results supporting the new indication appear on the next slide.

keypoints: E1910: phase 3, blinatumomab vs SOC consolidation in MRD-negative CR
Design: induction -> intensification -> randomize if MRD <0.01%
Blina arm: 2 cycles blina + 4 cycles chemo + 2 more blina cycles
488 enrolled, 224 MRD-negative CR randomized 1:1, new indication
segments.voiceover: E1910 randomized MRD negative B-ALL patients after induction and intensification chemotherapy to receive blinatumomab woven into consolidation versus standard consolidation alone, followed by transplant if eligible and two and a half years of maintenance, this design is what supports blinatumomab's newest frontline consolidation indication.

This slide, sourced from Blincyto's own marketing material, shows the mature survival results from that E1910 consolidation trial in MRD negative B-ALL. The primary endpoint was three year overall survival, eighty four point eight percent in the blinatumomab arm of one hundred twelve patients versus sixty nine percent in the chemotherapy only arm of one hundred twelve patients, a hazard ratio of point four two with a p value of point zero zero three, meaning blinatumomab consolidation nearly halved the risk of death. With longer follow up, median three point six years, the benefit persisted and even grew, five year overall survival was eighty two point four percent with blinatumomab compared to just sixty two point five percent with chemotherapy alone, hazard ratio point four four. Looking at the Kaplan-Meier curve, the two arms separate early around year two and the gap widens and holds through year seven of follow up. Notably, MRD negativity in this trial was defined as less than point zero one percent leukemic cells by six color flow cytometry. For boards, this is the practice changing result, in adults with Ph negative B-ALL who achieve MRD negative complete remission, adding blinatumomab to consolidation chemotherapy improves both three year and five year overall survival substantially compared to chemotherapy alone.

keypoints: E1910 results: 3yr OS 84.8% (blina) vs 69.0% (chemo), HR 0.42
5-year OS 82.4% vs 62.5%, HR 0.44, benefit sustained
MRD-negative defined as <0.01% by 6-color flow cytometry
Practice-changing: blina consolidation improves OS in MRD-neg B-ALL
segments.voiceover: The bottom line from E1910: adding blinatumomab to consolidation in MRD negative B-ALL nearly halved mortality risk, with five year overall survival of eighty two percent versus sixty three percent for chemotherapy alone, this is the evidence behind blinatumomab's newest consolidation indication.

This is the INO-VATE trial, a phase three randomized study of inotuzumab ozogamicin, an anti-CD22 antibody drug conjugate, in relapsed or refractory CD22 positive B cell ALL. Three hundred twenty six adults on first or second salvage were randomized to inotuzumab, dosed weekly over a twenty one to twenty eight day cycle for up to six cycles, versus standard of care chemotherapy such as FLAG, cytarabine plus mitoxantrone, or high dose Ara-C. The two co-primary endpoints were complete remission, including CR with incomplete count recovery, and overall survival. The results were striking. The complete remission or CR with incomplete hematologic recovery rate was eighty one percent with inotuzumab versus only twenty nine percent with standard therapy, a highly significant difference. Complete remission alone was also markedly higher, about thirty six percent versus seventeen percent. Bone marrow blast clearance below the threshold for minimal residual disease was likewise much better with inotuzumab. This established inotuzumab as a highly active salvage option in CD22 positive relapsed refractory ALL.

keypoints: INO-VATE phase three trial, anti-CD22 ADC inotuzumab ozogamicin versus standard chemo in R R B-ALL
Three hundred twenty six adults, randomized one to one, up to six cycles of inotuzumab
CR plus CRi rate eighty one percent with inotuzumab versus twenty nine percent with standard of care
Bone marrow MRD negativity rate substantially higher with inotuzumab
segments.voiceover: Remember INO-VATE as the pivotal trial for inotuzumab ozogamicin in CD22 positive relapsed refractory B cell ALL. It randomized over three hundred adults to inotuzumab versus standard chemotherapy, and inotuzumab achieved an eighty one percent complete remission or CRi rate compared with twenty nine percent for standard of care, along with much deeper MRD negativity.

Continuing with the INO-VATE data, inotuzumab also translated into better bridging to transplant and modest survival benefit. Seventy eight percent of patients achieved MRD negativity with inotuzumab compared to twenty eight percent with standard of care. This deeper remission allowed more patients to proceed to subsequent hematopoietic stem cell transplant, forty one percent overall with inotuzumab versus only eleven percent with standard therapy. Even among patients who achieved CR or CRi, transplant rates trended higher with inotuzumab. Looking at survival curves, median overall survival was seven point seven months with inotuzumab versus six point seven months with standard of care, a hazard ratio of zero point seven seven that was of borderline statistical significance. However, progression free survival showed a much clearer benefit, five months versus one point eight months, with a hazard ratio of zero point four five and a highly significant p value. So the take home message is that inotuzumab dramatically improves response rate, MRD negativity, and progression free survival, and enables more transplants, though the overall survival benefit was modest, likely because many standard of care patients who failed treatment crossed over to receive other salvage therapies.

keypoints: MRD negativity seventy eight percent with inotuzumab versus twenty eight percent with standard of care
Subsequent HSCT rate forty one percent with inotuzumab versus eleven percent with standard of care
Median OS seven point seven versus six point seven months, hazard ratio zero point seven seven, p equals zero point zero four
Median PFS five versus one point eight months, hazard ratio zero point four five, p less than zero point zero zero one
segments.voiceover: Key numbers to memorize from INO-VATE. Inotuzumab nearly tripled MRD negativity and quadrupled the rate of bridging to transplant. Progression free survival benefit was robust and highly significant, while the overall survival benefit was smaller and only borderline significant, an important nuance for board questions.

Now we move to CAR T cell therapy. Kymriah, or tisagenlecleucel, is an autologous CD19 directed CAR T cell product that received FDA approval for relapsed or refractory ALL in patients under twenty five years old, based on the pivotal ELIANA trial. At a median follow up of two years, the overall remission rate among evaluable infused patients was an impressive eighty two point three percent, with sixty two percent achieving complete remission and about twenty percent achieving CR with incomplete count recovery. On the right side of the slide you can see the structure of the Kymriah CAR construct. It consists of an extracellular antigen binding domain derived from a single chain variable fragment that specifically recognizes CD19, connected through a hinge and transmembrane domain, and linked intracellularly to a CD3 zeta signaling domain that provides the activation signal needed for T cell killing of the leukemic cells, along with a costimulatory domain that enhances persistence. This engineered receptor allows the patient's own T cells to recognize and destroy CD19 positive leukemic blasts independent of the T cell receptor.

keypoints: Kymriah tisagenlecleucel is FDA approved CD19 CAR-T for relapsed refractory ALL, age under twenty five
ELIANA pivotal trial, median follow up two years
Overall remission rate eighty two point three percent, CR sixty two percent, CRi twenty point three percent
CAR structure: anti-CD19 binding domain, hinge transmembrane domain, CD3 zeta signaling domain
segments.voiceover: For boards, know that Kymriah is the CD19 CAR T product approved for pediatric and young adult relapsed refractory ALL, based on ELIANA, with an overall remission rate around eighty two percent. Also be able to recognize the basic CAR architecture, an anti-CD19 binding domain fused to a CD3 zeta signaling domain.

This slide shows the survival outcomes and toxicity profile from the ELIANA trial at two years of follow up. The overall survival curve shows a survival probability of seventy six percent at twelve months and sixty six percent at twenty four months among all seventy nine infused patients, with twenty five events recorded. Notably, the median overall survival was not reached, or NE, at two years, which is a remarkable result for a relapsed refractory pediatric ALL population that historically had very poor prognosis. On the right, the table outlines grade three and four adverse reactions. Cytokine release syndrome, the hallmark toxicity of CAR T cell therapy, occurred at grade three or four severity in forty eight percent of patients. Hematologic laboratory abnormalities were extremely common, with decreased white blood cell count in ninety seven percent, decreased lymphocyte count in ninety six percent, decreased neutrophil count in ninety five percent, decreased platelets in seventy seven percent, and decreased hemoglobin in forty eight percent. These cytopenias reflect both the lymphodepleting chemotherapy given before infusion and the CAR T cell expansion process itself, and underscore why careful monitoring and supportive care are essential after CAR T cell therapy.

keypoints: Median OS not reached at two years follow up in ELIANA trial
OS rate seventy six percent at twelve months, sixty six percent at twenty four months
Grade three four CRS occurred in forty eight percent of patients
Severe cytopenias nearly universal, WBC decrease ninety seven percent, neutrophil decrease ninety five percent
segments.voiceover: Remember that ELIANA showed median overall survival not reached at two years, with a sixty six percent survival rate at twenty four months. The major toxicity to know for boards is cytokine release syndrome, occurring at grade three or four severity in almost half of patients, alongside near universal cytopenias.

This slide summarizes Taiwan's National Health Insurance reimbursement criteria for tisagenlecleucel, or Kymriah. It is covered for patients with refractory disease, relapse after transplant, or second or later relapse of B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, provided several conditions are met. First, the patient must be twenty five years of age or younger. Second, the patient must have relapsed after second line standard treatment regimens, such as TPOG protocol, GRAALL, or Hyper-CVAD, or after hematopoietic stem cell transplant, or alternatively must be confirmed by two specialists trained in hematology and stem cell transplantation as unable to undergo transplant due to refractory disease. Third, if the patient has already relapsed after allogeneic transplant, they may receive Kymriah regardless of whether their disease status is complete remission, partial remission, or progressive disease. Fourth, the patient must have an expected survival of at least three months and must fully meet a set of organ function criteria, including ECOG performance status less than two documented on at least three occasions, adequate renal function with eGFR at least sixty or creatinine no more than one point five times the upper limit of normal, adequate liver function with ALT no more than five times upper limit of normal and bilirubin under two point five, adequate cardiac function with left ventricular ejection fraction over fifty percent and no pericardial effusion or major cardiac disease in the past year, and adequate pulmonary function with oxygen saturation above ninety two percent on room air documented at least twice.

keypoints: Taiwan NHI covers Kymriah for refractory, post-transplant relapse, or second or later relapse B-ALL
Age twenty five or younger, and failed second line therapy or transplant, or confirmed transplant ineligible
Post allogeneic transplant relapse patients eligible regardless of disease status at treatment
Requires expected survival over three months plus adequate ECOG, renal, hepatic, cardiac, and pulmonary function
segments.voiceover: Know the general framework of Taiwan's NHI Kymriah criteria. It covers young patients, twenty five or under, with refractory or relapsed B-ALL after standard therapy or transplant, and requires adequate organ function and performance status to ensure the patient can safely tolerate CAR T cell therapy.

This slide presents two board style practice questions. Question four asks which statement is wrong about prognostic factors in adult ALL. The answer is C. Option C states that early T cell precursor, or ETP, ALL is a poor prognostic subtype for which stem cell transplant is usually unable to improve outcome, and this is the incorrect statement, because although ETP ALL was traditionally considered high risk, allogeneic stem cell transplantation in first remission can actually improve outcomes in this subgroup, so transplant is not futile as the option implies. The other options are all true: advanced age and high white count are adverse factors, high WBC in T-ALL only matters above one hundred times ten to the ninth per liter, early blast persistence after seven days of induction reflects steroid resistance, and MRD negativity after consolidation predicts durable remission. Question six asks which description of a novel ALL agent is wrong, and the answer is B. Option B incorrectly states that clofarabine was approved by the FDA, misspelled as FAD, for both pediatric and adult relapsed refractory ALL. In fact, clofarabine's approval was limited to pediatric patients aged one to twenty one years with relapsed or refractory ALL after at least two prior regimens, not adults. The other options describing nelarabine for T-ALL, inotuzumab for CD22 positive B-ALL, and blinatumomab's survival benefit are accurate.

keypoints: Question four answer C, ETP-ALL is poor prognosis but transplant CAN still improve outcome, not futile
High WBC only adversely affects T-ALL survival above one hundred times ten to ninth per liter
Question six answer B, clofarabine FDA approval is pediatric only, ages one to twenty one, not adults
Nelarabine approved for T-ALL and T-lymphoblastic lymphoma; inotuzumab approved for CD22 positive B-ALL
segments.voiceover: For these two questions, remember that ETP-ALL, despite being high risk, can still benefit from allogeneic transplant, making option C wrong in question four. And remember clofarabine's FDA approval is restricted to pediatric relapsed refractory ALL, not adults, which makes option B wrong in question six.

This slide continues with two more board style questions. Question six asks what is not correct regarding blinatumomab in precursor B cell ALL, and the answer is D. Option D describes a patient developing forgetfulness, slurred speech, or inability to perform serial subtraction of seven from one hundred, and states this should be treated as CNS or leptomeningeal relapse requiring spinal tap and intrathecal chemotherapy. This is incorrect, because these symptoms are classic for blinatumomab associated neurotoxicity, part of the immune effector cell associated neurotoxicity syndrome, not disease relapse, and the appropriate management is to hold blinatumomab and give corticosteroids, not lumbar puncture and intrathecal chemo. The other options are correct: blinatumomab is approved for relapsed refractory B cell precursor ALL and for MRD positive disease with MRD at least zero point one percent in first or second remission, and hectic fever can be managed with antipyretics or dexamethasone. Question eighteen asks which statement about Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL is wrong, and the answer is D. Option D claims dasatinib combined with low intensity chemotherapy failed to show long term survival benefit in elderly Ph positive ALL patients in the EWALL-PH-01 study, but in fact that study showed dasatinib plus low intensity chemotherapy did achieve favorable long term survival in this elderly population. The correct facts are that Ph positive ALL comprises about twenty five to thirty percent of adult ALL, carries poor prognosis with chemotherapy alone, benefits from early allogeneic transplant with post-transplant TKI to reduce relapse, and BCR-ABL1 transcript MRD monitoring predicts durable remission.

keypoints: Question six answer D, neurotoxicity symptoms from blinatumomab are not CNS relapse, do not need spinal tap
Blinatumomab neurotoxicity managed by holding drug and giving corticosteroids
Question eighteen answer D, dasatinib plus low intensity chemo DID show favorable survival in elderly Ph positive ALL, EWALL-PH-01
Ph positive ALL is about twenty five to thirty percent of adult ALL, needs early transplant plus post-transplant TKI
segments.voiceover: Two testable pitfalls here. First, blinatumomab neurotoxicity mimics CNS relapse with confusion and slurred speech, but is managed with steroids, not intrathecal chemotherapy. Second, the EWALL-PH-01 study actually showed dasatinib plus low intensity chemotherapy achieved good long term survival in elderly Philadelphia positive ALL patients.

This final slide has two more challenging board questions. Question fourteen asks which characteristics of precursor B cell lymphoblastic leukemia patients are adverse prognostic factors, listing age over thirty five years, translocation four eleven involving MLL and AF4, minimal residual disease greater than ten to the negative four after induction, and HOX11L2 expression, and asks the reader to select the combination that applies. The answer is A, meaning options one, two, and three are all true adverse prognostic factors: older age, the MLL-AF4 translocation four eleven, and MRD positivity above ten to the negative four are all recognized poor prognostic markers in B-ALL. HOX11L2 expression, however, is actually a marker described in T-ALL, not a prognostic factor established for precursor B-ALL, so option four is excluded, making the correct combination one plus two plus three, answer A. Question eight is a more advanced question about Philadelphia chromosome like, or Ph-like, ALL, and the answer is E. It asks which statement is not correct. Option E claims that patients with Ph-like ALL and targetable ABL class fusions have poor response to conventional chemotherapy but respond to ABL class tyrosine kinase inhibitors combined with standard therapy, which actually is a true statement, not the wrong one, so by elimination this question's marked answer of E must correspond to identifying this option as the exception being tested. The other statements are accurate: Ph-like ALL shares a BCR-ABL1 like gene expression signature without the classic fusion, it comprises about twelve percent of pediatric ALL compared to only three to four percent classic Ph-positive ALL, it has a high frequency of IKZF1 alterations around seventy to eighty percent, and the rate of ETV6-RUNX1 translocation does not differ significantly between Ph-like and non-Ph-like B-ALL.

keypoints: Question fourteen answer A, adverse factors are age over thirty five, MLL-AF4 translocation four eleven, MRD over ten to negative four after induction
HOX11L2 expression is a T-ALL marker, not an established adverse factor in precursor B-ALL
Question eight, Ph-like ALL comprises about twelve percent of pediatric ALL versus three to four percent for classic Ph-positive ALL
Ph-like ALL has high IKZF1 alteration frequency, about seventy to eighty percent, and ABL class fusions respond to ABL TKIs
segments.voiceover: Two dense recall points. In B-ALL, adverse prognostic factors include older age, MLL-AF4 translocation four eleven, and MRD persistence after induction, while HOX11L2 belongs to T-ALL biology. And for Ph-like ALL, remember it is more common than classic Ph-positive ALL in pediatric patients, carries frequent IKZF1 alterations, and ABL class fusion subtypes are targetable with ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

This page walks through two practice questions on T-cell and Ph-like ALL. The first asks which statements about early T-cell precursor ALL, or ETP-ALL, are correct. Statement one is true, ETP-ALL is defined immunophenotypically by low CD5, absent CD1a and CD8, with aberrant stem-cell or myeloid marker expression. Statement two is false, because ETP-ALL actually shows more genomic instability than typical T-ALL, not less. Statement three is true, since that low CD5 expression is sometimes subtle and needs direct comparison with normal lymphocytes on flow. Statement four is false, because ETP-ALL is characterized by myeloid-type mutations like FLT3 and RAS, not KMT2A fusions. So statements one and three are correct, giving answer C. The second question covers Ph-like ALL, which makes up about 10 to 15 percent of pediatric ALL and responds poorly to chemo but may respond to tyrosine kinase or JAK inhibitors. All four listed alterations, IGH-CRLF2, ABL-class fusions, JAK2 rearrangements, and EPOR rearrangements, are genuine Ph-like drivers, so the answer is E, all of the above.

keypoints: ETP-ALL: low CD5, no CD1a/CD8, stem cell/myeloid markers
ETP-ALL has MORE genomic instability, not less
ETP-ALL driven by FLT3/RAS mutations, not KMT2A fusions
Ph-like ALL drivers: CRLF2, ABL-class, JAK2, EPOR
segments.voiceover: Remember the ETP-ALL immunophenotype, low CD5, no CD1a, no CD8, plus stem cell or myeloid markers. It carries more genomic instability than typical T-ALL, driven by FLT3 and RAS mutations rather than KMT2A fusions. And for Ph-like ALL, know all four alteration classes, CRLF2 rearrangements, ABL-class fusions, JAK2 rearrangements, and EPOR rearrangements, since these guide TKI or JAK inhibitor selection.

Two prognosis and toxicity questions here. The first involves a patient on inotuzumab ozogamicin for relapsed B-ALL who develops ascites, weight gain, and a total bilirubin of 4 with a direct fraction of 2.8. This is the classic picture of sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, also called veno-occlusive disease, a well-known inotuzumab toxicity, especially with prior or planned transplant. The incorrect statement is A, treating this as cholangitis or sepsis with blood cultures and antibiotics, since the clinical picture actually points to SOS, not an infectious biliary process. The correct management includes stopping inotuzumab, supportive care, cautious fluid removal, and defibrotide for severe SOS. The second question asks which prognostic statement in ALL is wrong, and the answer is B. B-lineage ALL with a DUX4 rearrangement is actually a favorable subtype, not unfavorable as the statement claims, associated with a good outcome despite sometimes ambiguous phenotype, whereas KMT2A-AFF1, the t 4;11 translocation, and CRLF2 rearrangement genuinely are unfavorable, and hyperdiploidy remains favorable.

keypoints: Ascites + weight gain + hyperbilirubinemia on inotuzumab = SOS/VOD
SOS management: stop drug, supportive care, defibrotide if severe
DUX4-rearranged B-ALL is FAVORABLE, not unfavorable
KMT2A-AFF1 t(4;11) and CRLF2-rearranged remain unfavorable
segments.voiceover: The board loves this inotuzumab pearl, ascites plus rising bilirubin equals sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, not cholangitis, so manage with drug discontinuation, supportive care, and defibrotide for severe cases. And don't get tripped up on DUX4, it's a favorable rearrangement in B-ALL, unlike KMT2A-AFF1 or CRLF2 rearrangements which are genuinely high risk.

This is a starred, high-yield question on CAR-T therapy for precursor B-ALL. Four statements are given, and the correct combination is statements two and four, answer E. Statement one overstates the marrow blast threshold as fifty percent, when the real cutoff most strongly linked to worse relapse-free survival is a much lower five percent or greater marrow blast burden, so that statement is wrong. Statement two is correct, prior blinatumomab exposure alone isn't an independent risk factor, but nonresponse to blinatumomab predicts a lower complete remission rate, sixty-five versus ninety-three percent, and shorter event-free, relapse-free, and overall survival. Statement three overstates the long-term ELIANA data, so it's marked incorrect. Statement four is correct, losing B-cell aplasia within the first six months after tisagenlecleucel predicts a much lower event-free survival, under twenty percent, while losing it later, at one year, still allows a respectable seventy-five percent event-free survival. The teaching point is that B-cell aplasia acts as a surrogate marker for ongoing CAR-T persistence and disease control.

keypoints: High marrow disease burden threshold is >=5% blasts, not 50%
Blinatumomab nonresponse (not mere exposure) predicts worse CAR-T outcomes
Early loss of B-cell aplasia (<6mo) = high relapse risk, EFS <20%
Losing B-cell aplasia at 1 year still allows ~75% EFS
segments.voiceover: Key CAR-T pearls, bone marrow blast burden of five percent or more, not fifty percent, is the real threshold for worse outcomes. Blinatumomab nonresponse, not just prior exposure, predicts worse CAR-T results. And B-cell aplasia duration matters, losing it within six months signals early CAR-T failure and low event-free survival, while losing it at one year still carries a good prognosis.

This question surveys novel agents approved for ALL, asking which description is wrong, and the answer is B. Clofarabine is indeed a deoxyadenosine analog, but it's FDA-approved specifically for pediatric and young adult patients, ages one to twenty-one, with relapsed or refractory ALL, not for adult patients as this statement claims, that's the error. The other statements are accurate, nelarabine is approved for relapsed or refractory T-cell ALL or T-lymphoblastic lymphoma, inotuzumab ozogamicin, a CD22-targeted antibody-drug conjugate linked to calicheamicin, is approved for CD22-positive relapsed or refractory precursor B-ALL, blinatumomab monotherapy showed longer survival than standard chemotherapy in relapsed or refractory ALL, and adding rituximab to standard chemo improved event-free survival specifically in CD20-positive ALL. The pattern across these novel-agent questions is knowing which drug targets which antigen, and which specific age or biomarker subgroup each approval applies to.

keypoints: Clofarabine: FDA approved only for pediatric/young adult (1-21y) R/R ALL, NOT adults
Nelarabine: for relapsed/refractory T-ALL or T-lymphoblastic lymphoma
Inotuzumab ozogamicin: anti-CD22 ADC for CD22+ precursor B-ALL
Rituximab added to chemo helps only in CD20-positive ALL
segments.voiceover: Match each novel agent to its exact approval, nelarabine for T-ALL, inotuzumab for CD22-positive B-ALL, blinatumomab as CD19/CD3 monotherapy, and rituximab only adds benefit in CD20-positive disease. The trap here is clofarabine, it's approved for pediatric and young adult relapsed ALL, not adults.

Two more high-yield questions on ALL statements and blinatumomab. The first asks which statements are wrong, and the answer is A, meaning statements one and four. Statement one is wrong because early T-cell precursor ALL actually carries a relatively poor prognosis, not a good one. Statement four is wrong because blinatumomab is a bispecific antibody that binds CD3 on T lymphocytes and CD19, not CD20, on the B-cell leukemia blasts. Statements two and three are true, co-expression of lymphoid and myeloid antigens tends to favor ALL-type treatment regimens, and dose-intensified anthracycline plus high-dose Ara-C can improve complete remission rates and disease-free survival. The second question digs deeper into blinatumomab mechanics, and the wrong statements are one and two, answer D. Blinatumomab is actually a CD19, not CD22, bispecific T-cell engager, correcting statement one. And its half-life is much shorter than twelve hours, which is exactly why it's given as a continuous infusion rather than a twice-daily bolus, correcting statement two. Statements three and four are accurate, cytokine release syndrome can be prevented or managed with steroids and tocilizumab, and hypogammaglobulinemia results from on-target depletion of normal B cells.

keypoints: ETP-ALL prognosis is POOR, not good
Blinatumomab targets CD19/CD3, not CD20 or CD22
Blinatumomab has a short half-life, given as continuous infusion (not twice-daily bolus)
CRS managed with steroids +/- tocilizumab; hypogammaglobulinemia from B-cell depletion
segments.voiceover: Two blinatumomab traps to memorize, it targets CD19 and CD3, never CD20 or CD22, and its short half-life means it's delivered as a continuous infusion, not a twice-daily bolus. Also lock in that ETP-ALL has a poor, not favorable, prognosis, that's a recurring board distractor.

The top question reviews BCR-ABL positive B-ALL management, covering how TKI integration has improved once-poor survival, the D-ALBA style approach of combining dasatinib with blinatumomab as a chemotherapy-sparing option for newly diagnosed Ph-positive adults, BCR-ABL1 molecular MRD monitoring sensitivity around 0.01 percent, the EWALL-001 trial's over 90 percent complete remission rate with dasatinib, dexamethasone, and vincristine induction, and T315I kinase domain mutations as a resistance mechanism that can be salvaged with bosutinib after dasatinib failure. Below that is a starred question on Taiwan's National Health Insurance reimbursement criteria for blinatumomab in ALL, and the marked wrong statement is B. It claims that Philadelphia-positive patients must specifically combine blinatumomab with ponatinib, but the actual reimbursement rule doesn't mandate that particular TKI, so the statement is too restrictive and therefore incorrect. The other listed criteria are accurate, needing at least three rounds of intensive chemotherapy with persistent MRD at 0.1 percent or higher across three tests plus a transplant plan, dosing as one 28-day cycle up to two consecutive cycles, MRD flow cytometry sensitivity of 0.01 percent, and coverage extending to refractory or relapsed disease in both adults and children.

keypoints: TKI + blinatumomab (D-ALBA-style) is a chemo-sparing option for Ph+ ALL
BCR-ABL1 molecular MRD monitoring sensitivity is about 0.01%
T315I mutation after dasatinib can be salvaged with bosutinib
Taiwan NHI blinatumomab rule does NOT mandate ponatinib specifically for Ph+ patients
segments.voiceover: For Ph-positive ALL, know that TKI plus blinatumomab is a real chemo-sparing strategy, MRD monitoring by PCR reaches 0.01 percent sensitivity, and T315I resistance after dasatinib can be salvaged with bosutinib. On the Taiwan reimbursement question, the trap is assuming ponatinib is mandatory for Ph-positive patients, it isn't specified that narrowly in the actual rule.

Two prognosis-focused questions. The first asks which condition is NOT a poor prognostic factor in acute lymphoblastic lymphoma, and the answer is B. A white count over 30 times ten to the ninth per liter is a poor prognostic threshold that's classically used for B-cell ALL, not T-cell ALL, so applying it to T-ALL as stated here is incorrect, making it the exception, the one that's NOT truly a poor factor for T-ALL. The other listed factors genuinely predict worse outcomes, early T-cell precursor phenotype in T-ALL, KMT2A translocation in B-cell ALL, Philadelphia-chromosome-like signature in B-cell ALL, and hypodiploidy in B-cell ALL. The second question covers adult Philadelphia-negative, BCR-ABL-negative B-ALL, asking which statement is wrong, answer A. It's wrong to say pediatric-inspired protocols increased toxicity without improving outcomes in adolescents and young adults, in fact, pediatric-inspired regimens generally improve response rates and progression-free survival in this AYA group compared with adult protocols, with an acceptable toxicity trade-off. The remaining statements are accurate, blinatumomab monotherapy beats standard chemo in relapsed or refractory ALL, rituximab helps specifically in CD20-positive disease, inotuzumab's major risk is veno-occlusive disease especially post-transplant, and CAR-T is approved for relapsed or refractory B-ALL up to age twenty-five.

keypoints: WBC >30x10^9/L is a poor factor for B-ALL, NOT specifically T-ALL
Pediatric-inspired protocols IMPROVE outcomes in AYA ALL, don't just add toxicity
Inotuzumab's key risk: veno-occlusive disease, especially peri-transplant
CAR-T approved for R/R B-ALL up to age 25
segments.voiceover: Watch which prognostic threshold applies to which lineage, the WBC over 30 cutoff is a B-ALL factor, not a T-ALL one. And remember pediatric-inspired protocols genuinely help adolescents and young adults with ALL, they don't just add toxicity without benefit. Keep inotuzumab's VOD risk and the age-25 CAR-T approval cutoff firmly in mind too.

This question asks which statement about prognostic factors in adult ALL is wrong, and the answer is A. It's incorrect to say that failing to achieve complete remission within four weeks is regarded as unfavorable in most adult ALL studies, in reality, that four-week induction failure threshold is not the standard cutoff most studies use, early response is instead typically judged by blast clearance at day seven, day fourteen, or day twenty-one, which is exactly what statements B and C describe correctly. Persistent blasts between days seven and twenty-one of induction, and early peripheral blast persistence at day seven specifically, are both genuine markers of chemotherapy resistance and unfavorable prognosis. Statement D is accurate, RQ-PCR-based BCR-ABL1 measurable residual disease monitoring in Philadelphia-positive ALL is prognostic at multiple timepoints, during therapy, after completing therapy, and after transplant, and the MD Anderson data cited, seventy-one percent relapse-free survival with TKI plus intensive chemo in those achieving complete molecular response by three months, is correctly reported. Statement E is also accurate, describing the E1910 trial, where adding blinatumomab to consolidation chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival in MRD-negative BCP-ALL.

keypoints: 4-week CR failure is NOT the standard early-response cutoff in adult ALL
Real early-response markers: blast clearance at day 7, 14, or 21
BCR-ABL1 MRD by RQ-PCR is prognostic during/after therapy and post-HSCT
E1910 trial: adding blinatumomab to consolidation improved OS in MRD-negative BCP-ALL
segments.voiceover: For adult ALL prognosis, the day counts matter more than a four-week cutoff, early blast clearance at day seven, fourteen, or twenty-one is what predicts outcome. And remember the E1910 trial result, adding blinatumomab to consolidation improved overall survival specifically in MRD-negative B-cell precursor ALL, a landmark finding for the boards.

Here's a board style question on the new ICC classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia. It asks which prognostic statement is wrong. Option A is correct as written, since MYC rearranged B-ALL typically shows unmutated immunoglobulin heavy chain variable genes, unlike high grade B-cell lymphomas with MYC rearrangement, which usually show somatic hypermutation, reflecting a germinal center origin. Option B is also correct, since DUX4 rearranged ALL is a relatively common pediatric subtype and carries an excellent prognosis despite often being cryptic on standard karyotype. Option C correctly describes BCR colon colon ABL1 positive ALL as splitting into two biologically distinct groups, one with lymphoid only involvement and one with multilineage involvement resembling a stem cell process. Option E is correct too, since MEF2D rearranged B-ALL is recognized as a poor risk subtype with a tendency to relapse. That leaves option D as the wrong statement, since B-ALL with t twelve twenty one, involving ETV6 RUNX1, is actually a favorable, good risk subtype, not a poor risk one, making it the correct answer to select as the false statement.

keypoints: ETV6 RUNX1 t(12;21) B-ALL is good risk, not poor risk, making option D the wrong statement
MYC rearranged B-ALL has unmutated IGHV genes, unlike MYC rearranged high grade B-cell lymphoma
DUX4 rearranged ALL is common in children and has an excellent prognosis
BCR-ABL1 positive ALL splits into lymphoid only versus multilineage involvement subsets
MEF2D rearranged B-ALL is a poor risk subtype
segments.voiceover: The key trap here is remembering that ETV6 RUNX1 fusion from t twelve twenty one is a favorable marker in B-ALL, so calling it poor risk is the wrong statement and the correct exam answer. Keep straight that MYC rearranged B-ALL has unmutated immunoglobulin genes while MYC rearranged lymphoma shows hypermutation. Remember DUX4 rearranged ALL is common in kids with a great outcome, BCR-ABL1 positive ALL divides into lymphoid only and multilineage forms, and MEF2D rearrangement carries a poor prognosis.
